title: UGC NET Paper 1 — 18 June 2024 (Shift 2)
description: UGC NET Paper 1, 18 June 2024, Shift 2. 50 questions, 100 marks, 60 minutes.
instructions:
1. Total duration of UGC NET Paper 1 is 60 minutes.
2. The paper consists of 50 Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs) carrying 2 marks each (Total 100 marks).
3. There is NO negative marking for incorrect or unattempted responses.
4. You can navigate freely between questions using the Question Palette.
5. Questions can be saved, marked for review, or cleared at any time before final submission.
6. When the countdown timer reaches 00:00:00, your exam will automatically submit.

Passage: According to a World Health Organization (WHO) report, about 80 percent of the world population uses traditional medicine systems in some way or another. Traditional medicine systems in India include Ayurveda, Yoga, Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, Sowa-Rigpa, and Homeopathy, collectively known as AYUSH. All these systems were formulated, practiced, and integrated into healthcare coverage to achieve safe and economically feasible methods.

In many countries of the world, medical pluralism is the norm because no single system of medicine can single-handedly address all health concerns, but an integrative approach incorporating the positives of each system can benefit mankind. A patient-centered and individualized approach is the trademark of traditional medicine systems. Increased global attention to Ayush systems enabled the signing of the Host Country Agreement for the establishment of the Global Centre for Traditional Medicine (GCTM) at Jamnagar, Gujarat.

Passage: According to a World Health Organization (WHO) report, about 80 percent of the world population uses traditional medicine systems in some way or another. Traditional medicine systems in India include Ayurveda, Yoga, Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, Sowa-Rigpa, and Homeopathy, collectively known as AYUSH. All these systems were formulated, practiced, and integrated into healthcare coverage to achieve safe and economically feasible methods.

In many countries of the world, medical pluralism is the norm because no single system of medicine can single-handedly address all health concerns, but an integrative approach incorporating the positives of each system can benefit mankind. A patient-centered and individualized approach is the trademark of traditional medicine systems. Increased global attention to Ayush systems enabled the signing of the Host Country Agreement for the establishment of the Global Centre for Traditional Medicine (GCTM) at Jamnagar, Gujarat.
